function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Here’s a quick cheat‑sheet for finding the perfect place to order a cake—whether you’re looking for a classic birthday treat, a custom design, or something gluten‑free or vegan. | Category | What to Look For | How to Find It | |----------|------------------|----------------| | **Local Bakeries** | Fresh, artisanal flavors; often offer custom designs & seasonal specials | • Google “cake shop near me”
• Yelp or TripAdvisor reviews
• Instagram hashtags like #YourCityBakery | | **National Chains** | Consistent quality, easy online ordering, sometimes free delivery | • Costco (online + in‑store pickup)
• Walmart Grocery Delivery
• Target (same‑day delivery via Shipt) | | **Online Marketplaces** | Wide variety of styles, direct-to‑consumer shipping | • Goldbelly (specialty & regional cakes shipped nationwide)
• Etsy (handmade, custom orders) | | **Food‑Delivery Apps** | Convenience, same‑day delivery, often have “Desserts” categories | • Uber Eats, DoorDash, Grubhub, Postmates – search “cakes” or “desserts” | | **Grocery Delivery Services** | One‑stop shop for groceries + baked goods | • Instacart (partner with local grocery stores)
• Amazon Fresh (some regions) | | **Specialty Shops** | Custom wedding cakes, themed cakes, dietary restrictions | • Local wedding planners’ recommendations
• Specialty sites like CakeBoss.com | | **DIY Kits** | Build your own cake at home | • Amazon (cake kits)
• Local craft stores | ### Quick Tips for Ordering 1. **Check Delivery Times** - Most apps show estimated arrival windows. - Some bakeries offer “pre‑order” for next‑day pickup. 2. **Read Reviews & Ratings** - Look for photos of actual cakes, not just generic images. - Pay attention to comments about packaging and freshness. 3. **Ask About Dietary Options** - Gluten‑free, dairy‑free, vegan, keto, sugar‑free—most bakers now accommodate. - Confirm ingredient lists if you have allergies. 4. **Custom Orders** - Provide clear instructions: flavor, size, theme, text, decorations. - Send reference photos if possible. 5. **Payment & Cancellation Policies** - Verify whether you pay upfront or upon delivery. - Check cancellation deadlines to avoid fees. 6. **Packaging** - Ask if they use insulated boxes or temperature‑controlled transport. - For fragile tiers, confirm they’ll handle with care. 7. **Tip the Delivery Driver** - Many apps let you add a tip automatically. - If you’re ordering directly from a bakery, consider tipping the courier. --- #### Want a Recommendation? If you tell me your city or zip code, I can pull up the top-rated bakeries and delivery options right now. Or, if you’re planning a big event, let me know the occasion, guest count, and any dietary constraints—I’ll suggest the best local or national providers that fit your needs.
